content: NIC tuning: Windows exposes per-adapter, per-driver tunables via NDIS 'Advanced Properties' (visible in Device Manager Adapter Properties > Advanced tab), backed by PowerShell Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty/Set-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty cmdlets. Properties are keyed by RegistryKeyword (standardized ones prefixed '*', e.g. *RSS, *InterruptModeration, *ReceiveBuffers) and the valid value set/range is driver-defined and enumerable at runtime -- NOT a fixed list across all NICs. Registry location is HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Class\{4d36e972-...}\NNNN per adapter instance, but instance index NNNN is not stable across reboots/reinstalls, so tools should resolve by adapter GUID/name at apply time, not hardcode index. TCP Optimizer / community guides commonly recommend disabling interrupt moderation for latency-sensitive gaming, enabling RSS for multi-queue distribution, and disabling offloads for CPU-bound throughput tuning, but explicitly frame these as tradeoffs, not universal wins.
